Alright, I've just finished a series of documentation edits in `docs/functions.md`. The changes were fairly extensive: I renamed the `Attention.forward` entry to `Attention.attend_selected`, updated the description of the RoPE length error handling, expanded the `build_rope_cache` docstring to include an optional `length` argument, and most importantly I revised the `Attention.__init__` documentation to reflect the new sparse attention indexer projections and the added `index_gate` scalar. I also updated the summary line that reports the total parameter count, changing it from “1,047,168 parameters at defaults” to “1,074,825 parameters at defaults (1,047,168 dense core + 27,657 sparse-attention indexer parameters across 9 attention modules).”

Now that the docs claim a new total of 1,074,825 parameters, I need to verify that the actual model implementation matches this number. The `count_parameters` helper in `src/mythosmini/model/transformer.py` is designed for exactly this purpose, and it’s already imported in the repo’s test suite. I’ll instantiate a default `ModelConfig`, build a `MythosMini` model with it, and print the result of `count_parameters`. This will let me confirm whether the code’s parameter count aligns with the updated documentation.

Beyond the parameter count, I should also make sure that my recent edits haven’t introduced any linting errors or type‑checking issues. The repository provides a `make lint` target that runs the project's linter, and a `make pyaot` target (presumably for “PyAOT” static analysis). Running these commands will surface any style violations or type errors that might have crept in while I was editing the markdown file.

Since I need to capture the output of all three checks (parameter count, lint, and pyaot) in one go, I’ll combine them into a single Bash command. I’ll first execute a short Python one‑liner that imports `ModelConfig`, constructs a `MythosMini`, and prints the parameter count via `count_parameters`. Then I’ll pipe the output of `make lint` through `tail -3` to get the final few lines (which usually contain the summary of lint results), and similarly pipe `make pyaot` through `tail -2` to capture its concise summary. Using `2>&1` ensures that both stdout and stderr are captured for the lint step.

All of this can be done with the `.venv/bin/python` interpreter that the project uses, so I’ll reference that explicitly. The final Bash command will be:

```
.venv/bin/python -c "
from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig
from src.mythosmini.model.transformer import MythosMini, count_parameters
print(count_parameters(MythosMini(ModelConfig())))"
; make lint 2>&1 | tail -3 && make pyaot 2>&1 | tail -2
```

Executing this will give me the concrete parameter count and confirm that the documentation is accurate, while also ensuring the codebase remains clean and type‑safe after the recent documentation updates. I’ll now issue this as a Bash tool call.
